messages:
elaine: Heads-up — ran into a weird routing edge in staging. If a request arrives with both `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (workspace-scoped) and an `X-Workspace` header (set by a proxy) + `X-Pool: dedicated-42`, the gateway currently picks the header route and sends to the dedicated pool. That bypasses the token->workspace check and causes a 403 at the pool layer (workspace mismatch).

raj: Ugh. We discussed a few variants in the past but I don't think we landed on canonical precedence. My vote: token-derived workspace should be the source of truth for tenant isolation. Headers can be routing hints only when token is absent or when token explicitly allows header-override.

samir: Agree on defaulting to token. Also we should emit a telemetry tag when header-vs-token mismatch happens: `routing.decider=header` vs `routing.decider=token` and `routing.mismatch=true`. That will help SLO/alerting.

marta: For Private endpoints (VPC) we should be stricter — we can't allow proxies to inject workspace header and route into a dedicated customer pool. That is a potential isolation breach. Proposal: gateway scrubs `X-Workspace`, `X-Pool`, `X-Tenant` unless the inbound connection is from a verified private endpoint or there is an explicit `x-routing-authorization` signed header.

elaine: +1. We saw an instance where our internal API gateway accidentally forwarded `X-Workspace` from an internal service and created a routing loop to the wrong pool. Scrubbing by default, allowlist by source IP/networks.

raj: Implementation sketch (order of evaluation):
```
1. If token present:
   a. Resolve workspace from token.
   b. If `X-Pool` header present and pool belongs to workspace -> honor.
   c. If `X-Pool` present but not owned -> reject (403) and emit mismatch metric.
2. If token absent:
   a. If connection from verified private endpoint and signed `X-Routing-Auth` -> trust headers.
   b. Else treat headers as hints -> route to shared/default pool.
3. Always scrub routing headers before forwarding to internal pools unless explicitly allowed.
```

samir: Nice. Also: quotas attribution must use resolved workspace (from token or verified header). If we let headers win in any case we risk charging incorrect tenant. Add check in billing middleware: `billing.routed_workspace == auth.workspace // alert if differs`

marta: For Console -> Rollouts UX: when we flip a rollout that changes precedence (e.g., enable header-override for a partner), show an explicit banner that describes risk and add a gating checkbox: "I understand enabling header-based routing may bypass token scoping for verified endpoints". Also include a link to telemetry dashboard showing `routing.mismatch` for the past 7 days.

elaine: ops question: Who owns the allowlist for private endpoints? Is that infra or security?

raj: Security should own the canonical list, infra can read and cache it. We should expose a small API: `GET /v1/verified-endpoints` for gateway to refresh. Cache TTL short (5m) and fail-closed if unreachable.

infra-bot: deploy scheduled: gateway/route-decider v2 -> staging at 2026-04-02T04:00Z. CI: passed.

elaine: Thanks — I'll open a PR with the policy doc and the small config patch for header scrubbing + telemetry tags. Can someone volunteer to add the billing assertion?

samir: I'll take billing assertion + alert rule.

marta: I'll wire the console banner + dashboard link as part of the rollout page.
